IS : 6302 � 1971

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR WHIRLPOOL BATH

o.

FOR E WORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution
on 22 September 1971, after the draft finalized by the Artificial Limbs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division Council. 0.2 The formulation of Indian Standards for artificial limbs, prosthetic and orthotic appliances and rehabilitation equipment has been taken up at the instance of the Advisory Committee for Development of Surgical Instruments, Equipment and Appliances, Government of India. 0.3 Whirlpool bath is a rehabilitation item used for giving hydrotherapy to the patients. Means are provided for heating water in the bath and a powerful jet of water mixed with air gives a whirl. This also provides a soothing massaging action for the injured limb. This bath is suitable for providing hydrotherapy for both upper and lower extremities. 0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on rehabilitation equipment. Other standards published so far in the series are: IS: 5143-1969 Adjustable wooden crutches IS: 5144-1969 Metal forearm crutches (Canadian pattern) IS: 5145-1969 Walking sticks IS: 5150-1969 Rubber tips for crutches and walking sticks IS: 5588-1970 Quadriceps boots IS: 5665-1970 Shoulder wheel IS: 5796-1970 Weight set, disc, for physio-therapy exercisers other than pulley arrangements IS: 5827-1970 Paraffin wax bath IS : 6069-1971 Sliding seat exerciser IS: 6099-1971 Invalid walkers IS: 6205-1971 Stationary cycle exerciser for adults 0.5 This standard contains clauses 6.5 and 9.1 which call for an agreement between the purchaser and the supplier.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off' in accordance with IS: 2-1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the requirements pertaining to materials, shape, dimensions, manufacture, workmanship, finish and safety for whirlpool baths. 2. MATERIALS

3. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 3.1 A typical arrangement of whirlpool bath is shown in Fig. 1 and 2. However, other arrangements fulfilling the requirements of this specification shall also be acceptable.

4. MOTOR RATING 4.1 The motor shall conform to IS: 996-1964�. The rated output of the motor shall be 370 Wand the rated speed shall be 2880 rev/min. It shall run on a single phase 50 Hz ac supply.

5.: CONSTRUCTION 5.1 The bath itself shall be fabricated by beading and soldering and it shall be leakproof. 5.2 The recommended minimum and maximum levels of water in the bath shall be clearly marked inside the bath. 5.3 A drain cock shall be provided in the bottom to facilitate complete removal of stale water from the bath and for cleaning purposes. 5.4 The heater shall be provided on the side near the bottom and shall be so placed as not to hurt the patient when the bath is in use. The thermostat adjusting dial shall appear on one of the sides. 5.5 The thermostat adjusting dial shall be provided with a metal cover capable of being locked to prevent tampering with the thermostat setting. 5.6 The quantity of water pumped out shall be controlable by means of a flap or some other suitable device. 5.7 The damper in the air-pipe in fully closed position shall not permit any air bubble into the jet. 5.8 The motor-pump assembly shall be mounted on the bath over a shaft and shall be capable of being turned and fixed at angle, if necessary. 5.9 One indicator lamp each of distinctly different colour shall be fitted in the mains input circuit and the thermostat circuit. The lamp in mains input circuit shall operate at all times after the bath is switched on. The lamp in the thermostat circuit shall glow only when the heating circuit is on. . 6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 6.1 The bath shall be polished bright. All mild steel fittings which are outside shall be either plated or finished by hot stoving enamel spray painting.. The plating shall conform to Service Grade No.1 of IS: 10681968*. If painted, prior to painting, the surfaces shall be degreased, rust-proofed by phosphating and then suitably protected by an anticorrosive primer, either by brushing or spray painting. . 6.2 With maximum amount of water discharging from the pump and the air damper fully open, a vigorous whirl shall be created in the bath, 6.3 The motor and the immersion heater shall be suitably insulated electrically from the rest of the bath. The leakage current shall be measured as in 40 of IS: 302-l967t. The leakage current value shall not exceed the permissible value stated therein.
*Spedfication for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on iron and steel first revision ). tGeneral and safety requirements for light electrical appliances ( third revision).

7

IS : 6302 � 1971
6.4 The entire bath, with the motor-pump assembly mounted, shall be completely stable and shall not have a tendency to overturn. 6.5 If specifically desired by the purchaser, the bath shall be supplied with castor fittings to make it mobile.

7. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
7.0 The precautions given in 7.1 to 7.3 below shall be observed during the use of the bath to prevent accident and damage. 7.1 The temperature of the bath shall be checked up with a thermometer every time before giving treatment to the patient. This is recommended because in the event of a failure of the thermostat to operate at the pre-set value, the bath will get overheated and will cause blisters or burns to the patient. 7.2 The water level inside the bath shall be maintained within limits marked inside by the manufacturer. 7.3 When treating a patient the bath shall always be placed on a rubber matting and the patient's chair or stool shall also be placed on the rubber matting to avoid electric shock caused by accidental leakage.

8. MARKING
8.1 The bath shall be marked with the following: a) b) c) d) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark. Heater rating. Thermostat rating. Rating of the electric motor.

8.1.1 The product may also be marked with Standard mark. 8.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the

Bureau of Indian Standards Act, .1986 and the Rules and Regulations made
thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

9. PACKING
9.1 The bath shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
